title: Voice vocabulary vs tags and quick chips; the chip editor commit

steps.path: Chat → Edit quick chips → the pencil on a chip
steps.headline: Keep the chip editor change (commit 7b41b47fe), or go back?
steps.changed: That change made the chip editor match a tag's edit box: names over the two boxes ("Name", "Message"), and the switch and buttons inside the same box. Before, the boxes had no names and the switch sat in a second box.
steps.notice: Yes keeps today's version; No puts back the one on the left.
steps.risk: You said this one is your call; nothing else depends on it.

steps.headline: Should Voice vocabulary save as you go, like tags and quick chips?
steps.today: You add or remove words, then press Save at the bottom (outside the box). Tags and quick chips save each change at once.
steps.problem: It's the one editor of this kind with a Save button, and closing without pressing it loses your changes.
steps.proposal: Save each word as it's added or removed; drop the Save button and the "No unsaved changes" line.

options.label: Save as you go
pros: Same as tags and quick chips
cons: No way to back out of a batch of edits

options.label: Keep the Save button
pros: Change several words, then commit once

steps.headline: How should you add a word?
steps.today: A text box with a separate "Add" button beside it, and a hint line "Press Enter to add".
steps.problem: Tags add from one box (type, then Enter or pick), with no button beside it; quick chips use a "+ Add a chip" chip.
steps.proposal: One box like the tag box: type a word, press Enter, it becomes a chip.

options.label: One box, Enter adds
cons: Relies on knowing to press Enter (the box's placeholder says so)

options.label: Keep the Add button
pros: Obvious for people who don't press Enter

options.label: A "+ Add a word" chip
cons: An extra click to start typing

steps.headline: Where should the explanation go?
steps.today: A box with no label at the top ("Add names, unusual words or phrases…"), then a labelled "Your words" box.
steps.problem: Once one box has a label, every box should; and you asked for grey explanations to sit under the box they explain.
steps.proposal: Move the explanation under the add box as grey words, so the popup is one labelled "Your words" box.

options.label: Grey words under the box
pros: Matches your "grey text under the box" rule
cons: Explanation is read after the words, not before

options.label: Label it "About"
cons: Two boxes for a small popup

options.label: Line under the title
cons: Three sentences is long for a title line

steps.headline: Should the word chips look like tag chips?
steps.today: Your words are plain chips with an ×. Tag chips carry their colour and an ×; quick chips are plain and draggable.
steps.problem: Three chip looks across the three editors.
steps.proposal: Keep plain chips (words have no colour), but give them the tag chip's exact size and × so the two read as one family.
